title: Ainekio system architecture
description: Ainekio OS software ownership, runtime processes, stored state and external dependencies. This map is not live deployment or health status.

groups.title: Clients and entry points
groups.description: Browser, terminal and Android interfaces for sending requests to Ainekio OS.
details: The browser sends requests to the Astro web server. The mh CLI calls the engine from a terminal. Android runs the interface and an embedded Node.js server on the phone.
These components belong to Ainekio OS even when they run on different devices.

groups.title: Ainekio OS
groups.description: Software system · clients, server, shared libraries, agents, state and training tools
details: This boundary identifies software belonging to Ainekio OS. It is not one process, one computer, or a replacement for the host operating system.
The browser interface, mh CLI and Android app are Ainekio OS clients. The web server is a Node.js process; Android has its own embedded Node.js HTTP server.
Core is a shared TypeScript library imported by the server, CLI and workers. It is not a separate engine server.
Finite agents execute as worker subprocesses. Active Operator, Environment Bridge, Terminal and Maintenance have independent persistent-service lifecycles. They still belong to Ainekio OS.

Stored profile information, durable work records, configuration and training artifacts belong to the system through their existing storage owners. Training tools are explicitly launched work, not another permanent server.

Body Control, robot hardware and configured inference providers are separate systems connected through interfaces. This map shows software ownership and configured relationships, not current deployment or health.

groups.title: Shared engine library
groups.description: TypeScript library imported by the server, CLI and workers · packages/core/src/
details: The web server, mh CLI and agents call this TypeScript library inside their Node.js processes.
Collects the information for a model request, sends it to the selected provider, then runs workflows that process the reply.
Reads and writes profiles, conversations and memory. Tracks task progress, results and cancellation.
Connects workflows to speech services, tools and Body Control. Records what those calls return.
Code: /home/greggles/metahuman/packages/core/src/. Expand this group to see the individual functions.

groups.title: Agent system
groups.description: Shared coordination code plus separate worker and persistent-service processes
details: The catalog, trigger manager, monitor and execution code are shared infrastructure, not individual autonomous agents.
Finite agent families run admitted jobs in separate worker processes. Workflows compose work and are not themselves a permanent process.
The persistent services have their own Node.js processes and lifecycle. Being outside the web-server process does not put them outside Ainekio OS.

groups.title: Body Control
groups.description: Connects Ainekio OS and dashboard controls to the robot hardware.
details: A Python application that manages robot connections, sends commands, receives telemetry and serves the Body Control dashboard.
Its environment adapter accepts Ainekio OS actions. GatewayService sends commands to the selected robot. Freestyle turns movement requests into programs.
Can run beside Ainekio OS on the desktop or on the computer near the robot, such as Q6A.
Code: /home/greggles/Ainekio/Master/gateway/. The Freestyle generator runs as a separate HTTP service.

groups.title: Ainekio V2 body
groups.description: The physical robot: controller, microphone, camera, sensors, display, speaker and servos.
details: The ESP32-P4 controller receives commands from Body Control and drives the body hardware.
Microphone audio, camera images, IMU readings and joint feedback travel back through Body Control.
Hardware specifications and firmware are kept in /home/greggles/Ainekio/. The map describes the design and code; it does not certify installed hardware or physical operation.

groups.title: Configured inference services
groups.description: Services that run models for text, images, embeddings, transcription and speech.
details: Ainekio OS sends requests to the provider assigned to each model role. Body Control's Freestyle generator calls its configured motion model.
Addresses shown here are configured endpoints. A listed service may be stopped. Loopback addresses refer to the computer making the request.

groups.title: llama.cpp
groups.description: One host service exposes the configured local language, vision, motion and embedding models.
details: Clients select a model alias through the shared HTTP API. Native llama.cpp workers load and run that model with its own settings.
On one computer, Ainekio OS and Freestyle share this service. When Body Control runs on Q6A, its generator uses Q6A's own service.
Systemd runs llama-cpp.service. Host model settings are kept in ~/.config/llama.cpp/models.ini; bin/llama-cpp-services installs and starts the service.

groups.title: Other configured providers
groups.description: Alternative model backends: Codex sessions, Ollama and RunPod.
details: Model assignments select the backend for a request. Each provider client sends the request using that backend's protocol and returns its output.
These entries show configured choices, not three services used for every request.

groups.title: Speech conversion
groups.description: Whisper turns recorded speech into text; Kokoro turns text into spoken audio.
details: Ainekio OS's speech clients call these HTTP services and return transcripts or generated audio.
Audio playback is handled by the selected browser, computer or robot output.

groups.title: Stored state and configuration
groups.description: Saved profiles, work records, configuration and training files.
details: These are files and databases read and written by the components connected to them.
Profile storage can be local or on configured storage. path-builder.ts and storage-client.ts resolve its location and access.

groups.title: Training and evaluation tools
groups.description: Tools that turn reviewed examples into model candidates and measure their results.
details: Personalization training uses profile-owned examples. Action-selector training uses its own dataset and evaluation cases.
Each launched job produces datasets, reports or model files. Deployment and model selection are separate steps.
Code: /home/greggles/metahuman/brain/training/. Core starts personalization jobs through training-launch.ts.

nodes.title: Human
nodes.description: The person using Ainekio OS and the robot.
details: Types messages or commands, uses dashboard controls, or speaks into the robot microphone.
Receives text replies, spoken replies, task results and status reports. Sees the robot move and respond.

nodes.title: Web interface
nodes.description: The on-screen controls for chat, tasks, agents, voice, training and settings.
details: Runs the Svelte interface in the user's browser. Sends button clicks and messages to the Ainekio OS web server and displays the replies.
Shows task progress and system status. Also provides terminal sessions and configuration screens.
Interface code: /home/greggles/metahuman/apps/site/src/. The browser runs on the user's device.

nodes.title: mh terminal CLI
nodes.description: The mh command-line app: chat, manage tasks and agents, search memory and check status.
details: Accepts commands and typed messages in a terminal. Prints replies, results and errors.
Runs in Node.js and calls the Ainekio OS engine directly.
Code: /home/greggles/metahuman/packages/cli/src/. bin/mh launches entry.ts; main.ts selects the command handler from commands/.
Run ./bin/mh help from /home/greggles/metahuman/ to list commands.

nodes.title: Ainekio OS web server
nodes.description: Sends the interface to the browser and handles its requests using the Ainekio OS engine.
details: An Astro application running in Node.js on the Ainekio OS host.
Receives page and API requests. Checks API login sessions, calls the requested engine functions and returns pages, data or audio.
At startup, starts the engine's work queue, configured operating mode and model-service connections.
Code: /home/greggles/metahuman/apps/site/. Pages are in src/pages/; API routes are in src/pages/api/; src/middleware.ts handles API sessions and startup.
Development command: pnpm --dir apps/site dev. Production launcher: start.sh.

nodes.title: Application entry points
nodes.description: Receives API requests and exposes engine functions to the CLI and agents.
details: Web and Android requests enter through the API adapters and router, which select the matching handler.
Node.js callers, including the CLI and agents, import engine functions through index.ts or the relevant module.
Handlers pass work to the engine component responsible for it and return that component's result or error.

nodes.title: Tasks and execution records
nodes.description: Queues work and saves its progress, results and delivery records.
details: Accepts jobs from API handlers, triggers, workflows and agents. The queue selects a handler to run each job.
Durable execution records track work across process restarts, including cancellation and results that still need to be delivered.
Records distinguish submitted work from completed work and retain the returned outcome.

nodes.title: AI workflow execution
nodes.description: Runs saved graphs by passing each node's output to the connected nodes.
details: Loads a graph definition and its registered node implementations. Supplies the run's inputs and user context.
Executes the connected operations, such as building model input, calling a provider or sending a robot action.
Returns graph outputs and execution errors to the caller.

nodes.title: Model routing
nodes.description: Chooses the provider, model and adapter assigned to a request.
details: Resolves the requested model role against the user's model registry and settings.
Builds the provider request with the selected model alias and any request-specific LoRA adapters.
Returns the provider's response. Native services handle loading and running model weights.

nodes.title: Profiles and access
nodes.description: Finds the current user, validates login sessions and loads profile settings.
details: User records identify accounts. Session records connect authenticated requests to those accounts.
Profile functions load the selected user's settings. File access uses the configured profile paths and storage owners.

nodes.title: Context and persona
nodes.description: Builds the messages and other information sent to a model.
details: Graph nodes collect the selected conversation, memories, task information and persona data.
Their outputs form the model request's context. Which information is included depends on the graph and its inputs.

nodes.title: Memory and recall
nodes.description: Saves experiences and searches them for relevant information.
details: memory.ts writes profile-owned memory records with their source and event details.
vector-index.ts turns indexed text into embedding vectors and searches for memories related to a query.
Returns matching records to workflows, agents and user searches.

nodes.title: Goals and desires
nodes.description: Stores desires, their evidence, plans and review results.
details: Tracks a desire from its creation through review, approval, planning and outcome assessment.
Desire Agent and robot workflows read these records to choose or review work. Changes and results are saved against the desire.

nodes.title: Speech requests and delivery
nodes.description: Requests transcripts and speech audio, then sends audio to the selected output.
details: STT sends recorded audio to the configured speech-recognition provider and returns text.
TTS sends text to the configured voice provider and returns audio. Delivery code routes speech to browser playback or the robot connection and records delivery results.

nodes.title: Robot capabilities and feedback
nodes.description: Sends selected robot actions and records observations and action results.
details: Exposes the capabilities reported by the connected body to Ainekio OS workflows.
Sends requested actions through Environment Bridge. Receives camera and sensor observations, progress reports and final results through the same connection.
Keeps action identities so results and cancellations refer to the correct request.

nodes.title: Computer tools and sessions
nodes.description: Provides native tool execution and provider sessions for computer work.
details: Agent Mode delegates commands through the existing Full Task Delegation node and escalation backend.
The terminal code starts sessions, accepts input and returns output and exit information. The Terminal service manages those sessions.

nodes.title: Learning and model management
nodes.description: Builds training datasets, starts training jobs and manages saved adapters.
details: Reads reviewed training records and prepares the dataset for the requested run.
Starts training through training-launch.ts and tracks the resulting files and adapter information.
Model assignments determine which saved adapter is used for inference.

nodes.title: Agent Catalog
nodes.description: Lists available agents and which ones are configured to run.
details: Combines built-in agent definitions, installed source files, trigger settings and service settings into one list.
Reports each agent's name, purpose, source location and registration status to the UI and CLI.
Registering an agent adds its job settings to Trigger Manager; removing that registration removes those settings.

nodes.title: Trigger Manager
nodes.description: Submits agent jobs when their configured time, event or manual trigger occurs.
details: Reads trigger settings from etc/agents.json. Tracks when jobs are due and listens for matching events.
Sends due jobs to the engine queue. The queue runs them and returns their execution status.

nodes.title: Agent Monitor
nodes.description: Reports which agents are running, their recent logs and recorded failures.
details: Combines process records, queued job status and audit logs for the agent screens and CLI status commands.
Shows running, completed and failed work so the user can inspect what happened.

nodes.title: Service process lifecycle
nodes.description: Starts service processes and records when they start, fail or exit.
details: Looks up a service entry point, launches it in Node.js and records its process ID and startup result.
Uses the process registry to track running services and their failures. Service settings are kept in etc/services.json.

nodes.title: Agent job execution
nodes.description: Runs a queued agent job and returns its result to the engine.
details: Core launches the matching finite agent entrypoint as a worker subprocess and passes the admitted job and user context.
The worker returns its result or error; Core records the outcome against the queued job.
packages/agent-runtime defines shared input and result types. Core owns admission, execution and cancellation.

nodes.title: Memory agents
nodes.description: Turns files and transcripts into memories, then adds tags and other metadata.
details: Inbox Ingestor reads files from the memory inbox and saves them as memories.
Audio Organizer turns completed audio transcripts into memories when requested.
Organizer adds tags, entities and metadata to selected memories.

nodes.title: Training agents
nodes.description: Prepares training examples and trains adapters from reviewed examples.
details: Curator turns memory records into training material.
Environment Training Curator reviews saved robot attempts and proposes corrections for human approval.
Environment Training Trainer fits adapters from reviewed intent and task examples, evaluates them and exports GGUF LoRA files.

nodes.title: Thought and dreaming agents
nodes.description: Writes reflections, connected thoughts and dream narratives from saved information.
details: Mind Wandering (Reflector) generates reflections when selected by Active Operator or explicitly invoked.
Train of Thought follows a supplied thought or memory through related memories and saves the resulting reasoning chain.
Daydreamer writes short internal daydreams. Dreamer builds overnight dream narratives from memory fragments.

nodes.title: Curiosity agents
nodes.description: Generates questions and investigates them using saved information.
details: Curiosity generates questions for the user when selected by Active Operator or explicitly invoked.
Curiosity Researcher investigates pending questions and records findings from local memory.
Inner Curiosity generates and investigates questions as private inner dialogue.

nodes.title: Persona agents
nodes.description: Reviews conversations and memories to update persona information or select a persona facet.
details: Psychotherapist reviews recent memories and conversations, proposes persona changes and applies validated updates during Sleep or manual review.
Mood reviews recent conversation or inner dialogue and selects an enabled persona facet through the Mood Review graph.

nodes.title: Desire Agent
nodes.description: Creates and reviews desires, plans approved work and checks its results.
details: Reads attributed evidence to propose new desires and review existing ones.
Uses Desire Planner to build plans for selected desires, executes approved work and reviews the returned results.
Desire Planner is an internal worker called by Desire Agent.

nodes.title: Profile and body-event agents
nodes.description: Copies profile data between hosts and interprets incoming body events.
details: Profile Sync synchronizes profile settings, credentials and memories with the configured remote server.
Body Event Trigger passes a supplied body event, its measurements, Robot Status and the current task through its analysis graph.
These are two separate jobs grouped here for space.

nodes.title: Sleep Workflow
nodes.description: Runs memory review, training, desire review, dreaming and persona review during the sleep cycle.
details: Organizes memories, curates training examples, proposes robot-training corrections, trains a personalization candidate, reviews desires, writes dreams, reviews persona changes and rebuilds the memory index, in that order.
Saves whether the system is awake, sleeping or waking, along with the current and recent sleep sessions.

nodes.title: Robot Operator workflows
nodes.description: Builds robot context, proposes activity and reviews progress toward the current goal.
details: Robot Status combines telemetry, action history, conversation and desires into a situational summary.
Autonomy Controller evaluates the available operations. Goal Review checks the current objective against returned results.
Boredom Observer uses a fresh image to propose something to observe. Boredom Movement proposes a physical intention. Boredom Reflection proposes an intention from past memories.
Their outputs feed the robot execution workflows used by Active Operator.

nodes.title: Active Operator
nodes.description: Runs the robot autonomy cycle according to the selected operating mode.
details: In Reactive mode this service stays dormant. In Semi mode it selects activation updates at 100; in Full mode it selects the highest activation returned by Autonomy Controller.
Submits selected work to the engine's Work Coordinator and shared Environment workflow, then uses returned results in later assessments.

nodes.title: Terminal service
nodes.description: Runs persistent Codex conversations and Big Brother command-line sessions on demand.
details: Accepts session requests and terminal input. Returns terminal output and session status to clients.
brain/services/terminal.ts starts the implementation in packages/core/src/terminal/service.ts.

nodes.title: Maintenance service
nodes.description: Removes stale locks and old audit logs.
details: Checks for stale locks and refreshes agent status every five minutes. Applies audit-log retention at startup and once a day.
Runs as a background service; Trigger Manager handles agent job scheduling.

nodes.title: Environment Bridge
nodes.description: Carries commands and sensor feedback between Ainekio OS and Body Control.
details: Connects to the selected Body Control host and robot using the configured local, SSH or Cloudflare connection.
Sends actions and cancellation requests to Body Control. Returns observations, available capabilities and action results to Ainekio OS.
Also carries robot audio and speech messages over the connection.

nodes.title: Body Control dashboard
nodes.description: Browser controls for connecting, observing, calibrating and moving the robot.
details: Served by Body Control on port 8791. Shows camera images, sensor readings, joint feedback and command results.
Sends manual controls and configuration changes to the gateway. Motion executes on the host and robot, rather than inside the browser.

nodes.title: Environment adapter
nodes.description: Translates Ainekio OS actions into Body Control commands and sends results back.
details: Accepts the authenticated Environment Bridge connection at /environment on port 8790.
Translates requested actions for the selected body. Sends observations, advertised capabilities and correlated action results to the bridge.
Tracks action receipts and delivery acknowledgements so a reconnect can recover outstanding results.

nodes.title: GatewayService
nodes.description: Maintains robot connections and sends commands to the selected body.
details: Accepts authenticated robot connections at /robot on port 8790. Assigns session epochs and command sequence numbers.
Receives dashboard and adapter requests, sends commands to the robot, and collects telemetry and execution receipts.
Delegates description-based movement to the Freestyle executor.

nodes.title: Freestyle executor
nodes.description: Compiles a Freestyle movement program and sends its targets to the robot.
details: Receives a movement request and body observations from the gateway. Calls the generator when a program must be generated.
Compiles the returned program into body and joint commands, sends them through the gateway, and records execution evidence.

nodes.title: Freestyle generator
nodes.description: Asks the motion model to turn a movement description into a Freestyle program.
details: Receives a request over HTTP on port 8794, builds model input from the request and observations, and calls the configured llama.cpp model alias.
Returns a generated program or generation error to the executor. The executor handles robot transport.

nodes.title: Computer speakers
nodes.description: Plays speech through the Body Control computer's audio output.
details: Receives speech audio when computer playback is selected. Sends it to the host audio device instead of the robot speaker.

nodes.title: Microphone
nodes.description: Captures nearby speech as audio for transcription.
details: The robot microphone feeds the P4 audio system. Captured utterances travel through Body Control and Environment Bridge to Ainekio OS's speech input.
Whisper produces the transcript; the microphone itself supplies audio.

nodes.title: Camera, IMU and servo feedback
nodes.description: Reports camera images, body orientation and measured joint positions.
details: The camera supplies images. The IMU supplies motion and orientation readings. Servo feedback reports measured joint positions and feedback faults.
P4 firmware sends readings to Body Control, which makes observations available to the dashboard and Ainekio OS.

nodes.title: P4 firmware
nodes.description: Runs on the robot controller and drives movement, display, audio and sensors.
details: Receives commands over the robot connection and applies them to the body hardware.
Executes joint targets through the servo driver, updates the display and plays audio. Reports sensor readings and command results back to Body Control.
Firmware code: /home/greggles/Ainekio/Slave/firmware/esp32p4-wifi6/.

nodes.title: Robot outputs
nodes.description: Moves the joints, displays expressions and plays speech on the robot.
details: The PCA9685 and servos produce movement. The LCD shows expressions. The speaker plays audio received by the P4.
Firmware drives these outputs. Sensor feedback and execution receipts report what happened after commands were sent.

nodes.title: Native llama.cpp API
nodes.description: HTTP entry point for local model generation and embeddings.
details: Accepts a model alias and request data. Routes the request to the native worker for that model.
Text and vision requests return generated output. /v1/embeddings returns vectors for supplied text.
Model presets set GPU or CPU placement, model files and loading options. The service can run multiple native workers behind this one listener.

nodes.title: Qwen3.5 9B
nodes.description: Generates language responses and interprets images for assigned model roles.
details: llama.cpp preset alias: qwen3.5:9b. Receives text and, for vision requests, images; returns model-generated output.
The installed desktop preset offloads model layers to the GPU. Role assignments determine which requests use it.

nodes.title: Environment 0.8B
nodes.description: Runs small-model environment requests with the selected role adapter.
details: llama.cpp preset alias: environment-0.8b-base. Receives the prompt built by an environment workflow and returns generated output for that workflow to parse.
The request selects any role-specific LoRA adapter. Role assignments and graph configuration determine its job.
The installed desktop preset offloads model layers to the GPU.

nodes.title: Environment 2B
nodes.description: Runs small-model environment requests with the selected role adapter.
details: llama.cpp preset alias: environment-2b-base. Receives the prompt built by an environment workflow and returns generated output for that workflow to parse.
The request selects any role-specific LoRA adapter. Role assignments and graph configuration determine its job.
The installed desktop preset offloads model layers to the GPU.

nodes.title: Freestyle Qwen
nodes.description: Generates the movement program requested by the Freestyle generator.
details: llama.cpp preset alias: freestyle-qwen. Receives the generator's motion prompt and returns program text.
The installed desktop preset uses GPU offload. Freestyle compiles and executes the output through Body Control.

nodes.title: Qwen3 Embedding 0.6B
nodes.description: Converts text into 1024-number vectors for memory search.
details: llama.cpp preset alias: qwen3-embedding-0.6b. The embedding client sends text to /v1/embeddings and receives vectors.
The installed preset runs on the CPU with last-token pooling. Memory indexing and queries must use matching embedding settings.

nodes.title: Nomic Embed Text v1.5
nodes.description: Converts text into 768-number vectors when this embedding model is selected.
details: llama.cpp preset alias: nomic-embed-text-v1.5. Returns text embeddings through /v1/embeddings.
The installed preset runs on the CPU with mean pooling. Its vectors belong to an index built with the same model and dimensions.

nodes.title: Codex / Big Brother
nodes.description: Sends model work to a Codex app-server session through Big Brother.
details: The provider bridge sends the request to the local Codex integration and returns its response to the calling workflow.
Terminal service owns the provider session and its command-line process.

nodes.title: Ollama
nodes.description: Runs a selected model through Ollama's HTTP service.
details: Ainekio OS sends model requests to the configured Ollama endpoint and returns generated output to the workflow.
Ollama owns its model files, loading and inference process. Model assignments determine whether this backend is used.

nodes.title: RunPod Serverless
nodes.description: Runs selected model requests on a configured RunPod serverless endpoint.
details: The provider sends the request to the configured endpoint, follows the remote job and returns its output or error.
The endpoint ID and credentials come from configuration; the API base address alone does not identify a model deployment.

nodes.title: Whisper STT
nodes.description: Transcribes recorded audio into text.
details: The STT client sends an audio recording to the configured Whisper HTTP service and receives its transcript.
Ainekio OS passes the transcript into the speech-input workflow with its source information.

nodes.title: Kokoro TTS
nodes.description: Synthesizes spoken audio from text using the selected voice.
details: The TTS client sends text and voice settings to the Kokoro HTTP service and receives audio.
Browser playback or robot speech delivery sends that audio to the selected output. The map's Read aloud button uses the shared speech client.

nodes.title: Android app
nodes.description: Android interface with a WebView, microphone access and device speech recognition.
details: React Native opens the Ainekio OS interface in a WebView and handles native microphone permission and speech recognition.
The interface talks to an embedded Node.js server inside the app. The native bridge carries messages between web code and Android features.
Code: /home/greggles/metahuman/apps/react-native/.

nodes.title: Android local server
nodes.description: Serves the Ainekio OS interface and API inside the Android app.
details: Runs in the app's embedded Node.js process. Serves built interface files to the WebView and passes API requests to the shared Core HTTP adapter.
Resolves data paths for Android and connects the mobile agent handlers. Its local address refers to the phone.

nodes.title: Profile data
nodes.description: Stores each user's persona, conversations, memories and search indexes.
details: Profile functions, memory code and vector indexing read and write these records.
path-builder.ts and storage-client.ts locate the configured storage and handle access, including encrypted profiles.

nodes.title: Durable work records
nodes.description: Stores queued jobs, execution progress and results waiting for delivery.
details: Queue and durable-execution code write these records as work is submitted, runs, completes or is cancelled.
Recovery reads them after a restart. Delivery acknowledgements identify which required results have reached their consumer.

nodes.title: Configuration and workflows
nodes.description: Stores model assignments, agent settings and workflow graph definitions.
details: Resolvers and service owners read system and profile settings to select models, configure agents and find service endpoints.
The graph runtime loads saved node definitions and connections from cognitive-graph files.

nodes.title: Training artifacts
nodes.description: Stores training datasets, evaluation reports and candidate model or adapter files.
details: Training jobs write these files to their selected output or profile directory. Evaluation and deployment tools read them later.
A candidate becomes an inference model only when it is deployed and selected in model settings.

nodes.title: Personalization training
nodes.description: Builds profile training datasets and launches LoRA or full fine-tuning jobs.
details: Reads reviewed examples from the Curator store and prepares the selected user's dataset.
The Training Wizard and automatic-training policy call the same Core launcher. Jobs write training outputs and candidate model files.

nodes.title: Action-selector evaluation
nodes.description: Trains and tests environment action-selector candidates.
details: Builds training and evaluation folds from the system dataset, trains candidates and scores their outputs against evaluation cases.
Exports candidate adapters and reports. Deployment is a separate operation.

nodes.title: Conversation interface
nodes.description: Send messages to Ainekio OS and read replies, task progress and conversation history.
details: ChatInterface.svelte displays the conversation, message composer and response controls. CenterContent.svelte opens it as the Chat view.
Submits chat work through /api/unified-queue and follows task streams for replies and progress. Buffer streams supply updates for the selected conversation views.
Uses the shared microphone and speech playback code for voice interaction.
Code: /home/greggles/metahuman/apps/site/src/components/ChatInterface.svelte.

nodes.title: Workflow editor (Svelte Flow)
nodes.description: Edit workflow nodes and connections, save graphs and watch test runs.
details: Uses the @xyflow/svelte library to draw and edit workflow graphs in the browser.
Loads graph definitions and node schemas through the web API. Saves graph changes through /api/cognitive-graph and starts runs through /api/execute-graph-stream.
The engine executes the graph and streams run events back to the editor.
Code: /home/greggles/metahuman/apps/site/src/components/flow-editor/. FlowEditor.svelte draws the canvas; FlowEditorLayout.svelte loads, saves and runs graphs.

nodes.title: Architecture map (Svelte Flow)
nodes.description: Explore the system diagram, expand groups and read component descriptions.
details: This page at /architecture uses @xyflow/svelte to display the system map. architecture.json supplies its nodes, groups, descriptions and connections.
canvas-model.ts builds the visible nodes and connections. App.svelte displays the canvas and information panel. Dragged positions and expanded groups are saved in this browser.
Read aloud sends the selected information through the shared TTS client. The map describes the software; its diagram nodes do not execute workflows.
Code: /home/greggles/metahuman/apps/site/src/components/architecture-map/.
